newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds trade weaker, outperform after easing.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds trade weaker, outperform after easing.

text.p: Canadian bonds traded weaker on Wednesday, but spreads to U.S. bonds narrowed to 11-year lows, after Canada's central banks surprised many investors by cutting interest rates, dealers said.
"I think weakness is mostly due to the U.S. at the moment," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed-income analyst with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.10 to C$108.05 to yield 7.308 percent compared to the U.S. 30-year benchmark which fell 19/32 to yield 6.89 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to 42 basis points, the lowest since 1985, from 46 basis points at Tuesday's close.

The Bank of Canada surprised many in the market this morning when it cut its key bank rate to 3.75 percent, bringing the bank's target range for the overnight lending rate down to 3.25-3.75 percent. Analysts said the cut helped Canadian bonds to outperform U.S. bonds in volatile trading.
"If we don't see any strength in the numbers coming up then there's no reason to think they won't try to ease again," said TD's Bendiksrud.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent of 2006 fell C$0.17 to C$102.78 to yield 6.617 percent. The U.S. 10-year benchmark fell 11/32 to yield 6.60 percent.
The spread between the two shrank to an 11-year low of about 2 basis points from 4 basis points at Tuesday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded at 3.41 percent against the U.S. three-month bill at 5.17 percent.
